comment:
The terminology should distinguish pseudonymisation from anonymisation. Under the GDPR, pseudonymisation means processing data so that they cannot be attributed to a specific data subject without additional information; it is a safeguard, but the resulting data remain within the personal-data framework. The phrase “pseudo-anonymisation” is therefore both non-standard and potentially misleading. 

This distinction is also operationally important under the EHDS: personal electronic health data may be made available in pseudonymised form when anonymous data would be insufficient for an authorised secondary-use purpose, but access remains controlled through a permit and secure processing environment.

The terminology should distinguish pseudonymisation from anonymisation. Under the GDPR, pseudonymisation means processing data so that they cannot be attributed to a specific data subject without additional information; it is a safeguard, but the resulting data remain within the personal-data framework. The phrase “pseudo-anonymisation” is therefore both non-standard and potentially misleading. 

This distinction is also operationally important under the EHDS: personal electronic health data may be made available in pseudonymised form when anonymous data would be insufficient for an authorised secondary-use purpose, but access remains controlled through a permit and secure processing environment.
public.suggestedRevision: Replace “pseudo-anonymisation” / “pseudo-anonymised” throughout with “pseudonymisation” / “pseudonymised”. Add: “Pseudonymised data remain personal data where they can be attributed to an individual through additional information. Pseudonymisation is a technical and organisational safeguard and does not, by itself, establish a legal basis for secondary use. Data that have been rendered genuinely non-identifiable should be described as anonymised.”
